stance.label: Short-term bearish, nobody followed the bid at the prior low and ETF redemptions grew; long-term in the bottom zone

headline: Nobody followed the bid at the prior low: trading went quiet the next day while ETF redemptions grew to $453M; $60,000 holds only while sellers rest.
summary: Short-term bearish: the day after the break was bought back drew no follow-through, with volume at 38% of the prior day, another $453M out of the ETFs on Nov 25 and some of the chasing longs gone. Long-term bullish: total unrealized profit is down to 33.4% of market cap and the share of long-term holders at a loss sits just under this cycle's high. A close below $58,525 loses the prior low; ETF inflows and a close above $64,000 would show spot taking over.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 15 straight closes below; the close needs +18.9% to get back above

overview.lead: A thin Thanksgiving session: price covered only 2.8% all day and closed in the lower half of its range, and yesterday's high-volume lower wick still has no second candle to confirm it.
points: Close $60,499, high $61,533, low $59,850; volume was only 0.63x the 20-day average (Kraken).

US stocks were closed. More bad news on the AI side: Nvidia told server makers to halt shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, which gets priced in the Nov 27 half session (CoinDesk, citing the Financial Times).
Fear & Greed 11, the 14th day of extreme fear; November is -21.9% so far, and the worst November since 2013 was 2018's -37.0%.
Nothing new on the exit framework or the market stage; the close has been below the 200-day MA for 15 days.

cycle.lead: The long view is unchanged: the share of long-term holders at a loss is pressed against this cycle's high without making a new one, the miner-capitulation light is on for a second day, and difficulty goes up again today.
points: Long-term holders at a loss: 45.2%, against this cycle's high of 46.5% on Nov 20; a close below roughly $58,000 would exceed it (CheckOnChain; the level is an estimate).
MVRV Z 0.23 and NUPL 0.120, both inside the lowest 10% of the past four years (CoinMetrics, Nov 25).
The 30-day average hashrate is 1,006.6 EH/s, below the 60-day average of 1,014.8; today's difficulty adjustment is projected at +7.85%, so miners' costs are still rising (mempool.space).
The market stage is still bull, with 8 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA and the rule needing 30 to leave; none of the 6 supporting lights is on.

market.lead: Price is wedged between two piles of coins: $58,000–60,000 below changed hands only this week, $62,000–64,000 above is waiting to break even, and today touched neither.
points: Over 7 days the $58,000, $59,000 and $60,000 buckets took in 550K BTC combined while the $63,000 bucket lost 140K BTC (Bitview; on-chain moves are not necessarily trades).
The down leg has run 66 days and -30.1% on closes; it ends only with a close back at $67,627, which is 11.8% away.
The close sits at -1.55 standard deviations in the short-term holder cost band, with -2 standard deviations at $56,255 (Bitview).
The Sell Pressure Index has been at its maximum for 17 days and the bottom setup is in place; that setup has appeared 20 times since 2012, with a median further drop of 12% before it cleared.

deriv.lead: Some of the longs that chased yesterday left today, and they left quietly, with no liquidations; options are still buying downside protection, and only after today's monthly expiry will it be clear whether that insurance gets cheaper.
points: The weighted funding rate is 4.44% against 6.34% yesterday; market-wide open interest is 326K BTC and long liquidations for the day were only $13.2M (Coinalyze).

Longs held by the top 2,000 Hyperliquid accounts by equity fell from 9,491 BTC to 7,603 BTC in a day while shorts at 10,349 BTC barely moved (Hyperliquid only; large accounts may be market makers or hedgers).
7-day implied volatility is 2.9 points above 90-day, down from 4.9 yesterday; the 25-delta risk reversal is -6.9 and option premium has leaned toward puts for 29 days (Deribit).

The estimated long-liquidation band sits at $56.2–57.2K with 8,563 BTC; the short-liquidation band above at $64.6–67.6K holds 38K BTC (several exchanges, an estimate). The order book shows a $181M bid and a $174M offer at $60,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: Money is still leaving and has not slowed: this month's ETF redemptions are already the largest since launch and stablecoins are still being cashed out to dollars; the one thing that improved is US spot taker selling, which narrowed a little more.
points: Today's finding sits on this page: ETFs lost $453M on Nov 25, a 7th straight outflow; the 20-trading-day total is -$5.35B, only $290M short of this June's deepest -$5.64B (CoinMarketCap).

Coinbase 7-day net taker selling is 4,486 BTC against 5,011 BTC yesterday (Coinalyze); the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount was -0.005% on the day, so yesterday's positive print did not last.
Stablecoins $282.2B, down 1.05% in 7 days (DefiLlama); USDT trades at $0.9987 with a 7-day average discount of 0.162%, in the deepest 1% since the data began in October 2022.
Rates are unchanged as a headwind: Polymarket puts a December hike at 95.6%, and the 2-year Treasury yield is 0.61 percentage points above the Fed's upper bound (Nov 25).

onchain.lead: Loss-taking has come off its peak a little, and the loss-taking phase is not over: sellers as a group are in the red and short-term holders have sold at a loss for three straight weeks.
points: Network-wide 90-day realized profit ÷ loss is 0.982 against 0.993 yesterday, so the direction of yesterday's second finding holds (Bitview).
Long-term holders realized $4.08B of losses over 7 days, down from $4.38B yesterday; the LTH-SOPR 7-day average is 0.765 (Bitview).
Short-term holder loss-taking intensity is 1.34 against 1.91 yesterday, further from the threshold of 2; STH-SOPR is 0.987, below 1 for 21 days (CheckOnChain).

By address-balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 18K BTC in 7 days and the 100–1,000 BTC tier shed 15K BTC (Bitview); the long-term holder 30-day net position is -185K BTC, negative for 114 days (bitcoin-data, Nov 25).

exit.lead: Nothing happened on the exit page today; the nearest condition needs a rally of more than 80% to come into reach.
points: 15 straight closes below the 200-day MA at $71,920, 15.9% under it; the hedge buy-back condition was already met on Nov 17.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.409, with the 0.75 line at $110,448; the three top indicators read 7 / 6 / 35, all low (CoinMetrics, Nov 25).

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs lost $453.1M on Nov 25, a 7th straight outflow, with BlackRock's IBIT at $329.7M; November outflows of about $5.39B already exceed any month since launch
news.source: The Block, 2026-11-26 (SoSoValue data; Cointelegraph cites Farside at $453M the same day, with June's $4.51B as the prior record)
news.read: This site's source has Nov 25 at -$453.0M, so the three sources agree within $1M. Yesterday's edition counted the Nov 24 outflow shrinking to $235M as part of the selling easing; today we correct that: it shrank for one day, and Nov 25 was back at nearly twice the day before. Our 20-trading-day total is -$5.35B, only $290M short of June's deepest -$5.64B. Markets were closed on Nov 26, so the next print is the Nov 27 half session, and it decides today's finding.

news.title: JPMorgan: Strategy's share price to bitcoin NAV fell to a record low of 0.88x, signaling capitulation in BTC; IBIT outflows are more intense than from early May to late June, and its BTC production cost estimate is about $86,000
news.read: The capitulation it reads from a share price shows up on-chain here as well: network-wide 90-day realized profit is below realized loss and long-term holders took $4.08B of losses in a week. Capitulation describes how much pain sellers are in and says nothing on whether buyers have arrived; the bank itself notes IBIT kept bleeding during the bounce, which points the same way as today's finding. Its $86,000 production cost and this site's difficulty-based estimate come from two different methods and should not be netted. We record Strategy's holdings at a 19.8% paper loss (CoinGecko). No change to the cycle view.

news.title: About $7B of BTC options expire on Deribit on Friday, smaller than October's $10.8B; the put ÷ call open interest ratio across all expiries rose to 0.81 from 0.55 in October, with puts clustered at $60,000 and below
news.read: This site's Deribit ratio across all expiries is 0.791, the same direction, and option premium has leaned toward puts for 29 days. The expiry is at 16:00 Taipei (08:00 UTC) on Nov 27; after it the largest block is Dec 25 at 37.2% of total open interest, with the most puts stacked at $60,000. Heavy protection buying shows a market guarding against a drop and gives no direction. Whether 7-day implied volatility falls back under 90-day after the expiry will show if the tension has eased; it is still 2.9 points higher.

news.title: Nvidia told server makers including Dell and Super Micro to halt shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after the US tightened AI chip export controls (Financial Times); the Nasdaq 100 is down as much as 17% from its high and Nvidia as much as 50% from its October peak
news.source: CoinDesk, 2026-11-26 (citing the Financial Times and Bloomberg)
news.read: US stocks were closed on Nov 26, so this gets priced in the Nov 27 half session. This site's 30-day BTC–Nasdaq correlation is 0.745; over the last 60 US trading days BTC fell 116.9% as much as the Nasdaq 100 on its down days and rose only 83.1% as much on its up days. Another leg down in AI stocks would take BTC with it, and by more. This is macro backdrop and does not change the cycle view.

news.title: Hong Kong-based market maker Auros is reportedly winding down, with the reason and timetable unclear; in 2024 it estimated it handled about 4% of global crypto exchange volume
news.source: CoinDesk, 2026-11-26 (two people familiar with the matter)
news.read: One fewer market maker means thinner books, and how much depends on how fast others fill the gap. Across the 13 exchange order books this site tracks, resting bids near price are $308M and offers $307M, equally thick, so no gap shows yet. Thinner books let price travel faster in both directions, the same kind of risk as dealers being short gamma near $58,000 (an estimate). No change to any reading.

news.title: BTC unmoved for a year or more is 68.5% of circulating supply, up from 62% in July (Glassnode); the same rebound appeared in past bear-market bottoming phases, with little guidance on timing
news.read: This site's CheckOnChain-based count of supply inactive for a year or more rose 951K BTC in 30 days, the same direction; a large part of that is the one-year echo of the suspected 468K BTC wallet transfer of Nov 22–23 last year, so not all of it is a decision to hold. Over the same period the long-term holder 30-day net position is -185K BTC (bitcoin-data, Nov 25): more idle coins and net selling by long-term holders are both true. No change to any reading.

news.title: Switzerland's first spot BTC ETF (BBIT) began trading on SIX: a fund that holds BTC directly, a 0.19% annual fee and 350 BTC at launch; FINMA approved it on Oct 20 and it is offered publicly only in Switzerland
news.read: The launch size is a little over $20M, while US spot ETFs lost $453M in a single day on Nov 25, a different order of magnitude. One more regulated access point matters over years; it brings no immediate money and changes no reading.

actions.head: Don't read $60,000 holding on thin volume as the prior low being secure.
actions.text: It held on a day when US stocks were closed and volume was 0.38x the prior day, so nobody was tested. The ETFs have yet to post a single inflow day and the Nov 25 redemption was nearly double the day before; 73.8% of Binance accounts are long, and of the 26 times that share got this high, price was higher 90 days later only 10 times.

actions.text: Deribit's monthly expiry at 16:00 (08:00 UTC), about $7B; a difficulty adjustment projected at +7.85%; and a half session for US stocks, closing at 02:00 on Nov 28 (18:00 UTC), in which both the Nvidia shipment halt and ETF creations and redemptions get priced. The Nov 27 ETF flow decides today's finding.

actions.head: $58,525 below, $62,000–64,000 above.
actions.text: A close below $58,525 is a new low for this cycle; the estimated long-liquidation band sits at $56.2–57.2K, and below that is the realized price at $53,026 (Bitview). Above, $61,000 carries $83.4M of offers (Hyperliquid perps), and the $62,000–64,000 buckets hold 1.03M BTC of short-term holder supply.

changes.title: Volume fell 62% in a day

changes.fig: Weighted funding rate 6.34% → 4.44%; Hyperliquid large-account longs 9,491 → 7,603 BTC

changes.say: Nobody in Asia is paying up to get into stablecoins, and the Korea premium is still under its 1.14% median. The small Asian bid seen during yesterday's break is gone today.

changes.title: The gap between the two hashrate averages widened a little
changes.say: The miner-capitulation light is on for a second day and the ratio is a hair from the 0.99 set in the second finding of Nov 23. Hashrate over the last 7 days is still 5.2% above the week before; miners who cannot keep up will show after today's difficulty increase.

findings.title: ETF redemptions grew again: spot money did not follow the bid at the prior low
findings.lean_why: The largest channel for spot buying is still draining faster, and redemptions grew on the very day the break was bought back; sellers easing on the order book does not mean someone has taken over.
findings.what: The slower outflow we wrote about yesterday lasted one day: ETFs lost $453M on Nov 25, nearly twice the day before and a 7th straight outflow (CoinMarketCap, Nov 25).
findings.why: Start with which days, and whether it is a one-off. The 7 trading days add up to $2.57B of outflows, 3 of them above $450M; the $235M on Nov 24 was the low of the stretch and the next day bounced right back. The Block cites SoSoValue at $453.1M with BlackRock's IBIT at $329.7M, and Cointelegraph cites Farside at $453M, so three sources agree within $1M. The 20-trading-day total is -$5.35B, only $290M short of this June's deepest -$5.64B. Over the same days the exchange tape improved: Coinbase 7-day net taker selling narrowed from 5,011 BTC to 4,486 BTC, and the three spot venues were net taker buyers of 588 BTC on Nov 26 (Coinalyze). That contradiction is today's point: fewer sell orders on the tape, no fewer redemptions off it. The other channels have not turned either: stablecoins are down 1.05% in 7 days and the 7-day average USDT discount of 0.162% is in the deepest 1% on record. US markets were closed on Nov 26 with no ETF flows, price covered only 2.8% all day on 0.38x the prior day's volume, and yesterday's high-volume candle got no second one.
findings.alt: The other path is that the Nov 25 redemptions were panic orders from the day of the break: price fell to $57,211 intraday and creations and redemptions go in before the US close, so they reflect the mood near the low, while orders placed after the recovery only show up on Nov 27. The next print separates the two: an outflow back inside $200M or an inflow on Nov 27 makes Nov 25 the tail of the panic; another $400M or more means redemptions did not stop when price did. Data limits: ETF flows arrive a trading day late, and Nov 27 is a half session with lighter volume; taker flow counts only aggressive orders, and ETF creations and redemptions mostly settle off-exchange, so they need not appear on the Coinbase tape.
findings.history: ETF outflow stretches have never ended in a few days. Since the 2024 launch, 4 completed stretches saw the 20-trading-day total fall below -$1.5B, each lasting 19 to 40 trading days, and this one is on day 13. In this year's May–July stretch the deepest day was Jun 9 and the price low came three weeks later on Jun 30. Returns in the 30 days after a stretch ended went both ways.
findings.so: What changes is the weight of the 'selling eased' part of yesterday's first finding: only the exchange tape eased, the ETF side got heavier, and no spot money is yet holding price above $60,000. What does not change is the prior low, with daily closes still above $58,525; the close is 23.4% below the estimated cost basis of ETF holders, so that group is far from breakeven, and the long-term valuation is still in the bottom zone.
findings.next: By Dec 3: a 20-trading-day total below -$5.64B makes this stretch deeper than June's and means redemptions are still widening; a close above $64,000 would show spot pushing price through the trapped supply while redemptions continue, and refute this finding.

research.summary: JPMorgan's Nov 25 report reads Strategy trading below its bitcoin NAV as capitulation and notes IBIT outflows heavier than in May–June, in line with this site's view of deep loss-taking and absent buyers; 10x Research published a new issue on Nov 26 (paywalled). No new issue from Glassnode, Bitfinex Alpha or K33.

items.title: Strategy's share price to bitcoin NAV at a record low signals capitulation in BTC (as reported by The Block; the report itself is not public)
items.points: Read only through The Block's coverage: Strategy's ratio fell to 0.88x, below the prior low from late June; IBIT kept losing assets during the brief price recovery, more intensely than from early May to late June; estimated production cost is about $86,000, and the wider gap may push higher-cost miners to sell reserves.
items.meaning: The capitulation read matches this site's on-chain data: long-term holders took $4.08B of losses in a week and 90-day realized profit is below realized loss. Its IBIT observation is today's finding: our 20-trading-day total is -$5.35B, only $290M short of June's deepest.

items.title: Can Bitcoin Bounce Again, and Will It Last This Time?
items.points: Paywalled, title only: whether another bounce comes and whether it can last.
items.meaning: The body was not read, so no comparison. This site's answer today is that the bounce has no buyer yet: 7 straight ETF outflow days, and volume at 0.38x the prior day right after the break was bought back.

items.title: Bitcoin's Recovery Remains Elusive
items.points: ETFs lost $231.4M on Nov 24, the first day under $300M since Nov 17, which it treated as a first sign of easing; funding at 6–8% was read as leveraged longs buying; the base case is $56,300–61,400 into the Nov 27 expiry, and a turn needs three straight ETF inflow days, a hold above $61,300 and STH-SOPR back at 1.
items.meaning: Its first sign of easing was gone a day later: Nov 25 saw $453M leave. None of its three turn conditions is met here: 7 straight ETF outflow days, a close of $60,499 under $61,300, STH-SOPR at 0.987. Price is still inside its range. Nothing newer on the list.

items.title: The $14 Billion Decision Bitcoin ETF Holders Must Make by December 31
items.points: Paywalled, title only: a decision ETF holders face before year end, sized at $14 billion.
items.meaning: The body was not read, so no comparison. This site estimates the close is 23.4% below the ETF holders' cost basis and has been under it for 15 days; on whether this group sells before year end, the Nov 25 number points toward selling.

items.title: Strategy Watch #10
items.points: The October institutional monthly: BTC's 30-day net inflow peaked at $14.2B on Oct 17 and eased to $9.2B by month end; the 30-day stablecoin flow turned negative on Oct 7 and passed $6B of outflow late in the month; US spot ETFs ended October with a 5.6K BTC outflow, the first since July; average manager cash rose from 12.2% to 15.7%.
items.meaning: It covers October, and November's selling already had precursors then: stablecoins turned negative first and ETFs followed. This site now has stablecoins down $17.2B in 30 days and ETFs at -$5.35B over 20 trading days, both far deeper than its end-October figures.

items.title: The Week On-chain: The Canary in the Coal Mine
items.points: Selling intensified after the $62–66K support broke; realized losses are the heaviest since FTX in November 2022, called the first major capitulation of this bear market; ETF net outflows reached $4.3B over 20 trading days; dealers are short gamma at $58–64K; below a daily close under $60K and the June low of $58.5K, the next level is the realized price at $53.2K.
items.meaning: Its key level of $58.5K still holds on daily closes. It had ETF outflows at $4.3B over 20 trading days; this site now has $5.35B, about $1B more in a week. Our estimated short gamma is heaviest at $58,000 and the realized price is $53,026 (Bitview). No new issue; this is still the latest on the list.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 48
items.points: Weekly ETF net outflow of $1.7B, the heaviest since early July, with ETF holders' MVRV down to 0.97; futures open interest fell 12% to $29.3B, the lowest since early March; 25-delta skew rose to 17.4%, the highest since mid-July; supply in profit 47.3%, realized cap monthly change -0.93%.
items.meaning: It says leverage was flushed; what this site sees is that it has not been rebuilt since: open interest is 326K BTC, down 2.5% in 7 days, and part of yesterday's chasing longs left today. Our realized cap monthly change is now -1.84%, twice as deep as its figure.

items.title: What Comes Next After a New Cycle Low?
items.points: The Nov 21 low of $55,501 was the lowest since September 2024, after seven straight weekly declines; resistance at $61,300 and the short-term holder cost basis of $72,720, realized price $53,200; base case a $56,800–64,900 range into the Nov 27 expiry, with risk skewed toward a retest of $55,501.
items.meaning: A day before the expiry price is still inside its range, closing at $60,499; its first resistance at $61,300 was touched by today's high of $61,533 and not reclaimed.

items.title: Digital assets digest - November 24th 2026
items.points: The page carries only a headline and a download link: BTC near $60,000 and Fed risk. Its head of research told The Block on Nov 25 that the market is at the tail end of the bear market, with a $60,000–90,000 range and a breakout needing a monetary policy shift.
items.meaning: The close at $60,499 sits right on the lower edge of its range. The late-bear read matches this site's long-term bottom-zone view; a tail end can drag on, which is what our second finding of Nov 25 was about.

items.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
items.points: 13F filers added the equivalent of 49,229 BTC in Q3 and hold a record 356,491 BTC, 27.6% of spot BTC funds; advisers and wealth platforms make up 40.5% of that. Fund holdings fell 38,531 BTC from quarter end to Nov 16.
items.meaning: The wealth-channel clients who entered in Q3 are underwater as a group, and November's record outflow shows some are redeeming. Galaxy separately treats a daily close below $58,525 and a weekly close below $59,517 as the dividing lines (CoinDesk, Nov 26); neither has happened.

items.title: No gain, plenty of pain
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC broke below its 200-week MA, ETF exposure is back to mid-August levels and funding is negative; it argues these readings have matched BTC bottoms before.
items.meaning: The funding item on its list is positive now: 4.44% weighted, with a 7-day average of 2.44%. Nothing newer on the list.
